Every step, in writing.

This page is the whole structure: the timeline, the premium, the option, and the fine print. Read it the way you'd read a lease, slowly and with questions. Then bring us the questions.

Medre is a healthcare real estate company founded by a commercial real estate broker and a practicing physician. It buys the building a practice needs and leases it to the practice, with a written option to buy at year 5 or year 10, priced by independent appraisal at fair market value at the time of sale, with no personal guarantee and no down payment from the practice. This page walks the structure end to end.

The timeline

Five steps, start to deed.

1

The call.

Thirty minutes with Erika or Steve. We run your numbers against your market and tell you whether the structure pencils. If the better answer is buying a building yourself or staying put, we say so, and that's the end of it.

2

The search.

We find the right building for your practice, or evaluate the one you're in. You approve the location, the space, and the numbers before anything gets signed. If the building isn't right, we keep looking.

3
Purchase process agreed here

The close.

Medre buys the building with our capital and our mortgage. Your lease and your written purchase option are signed the same day. The option names year 5 and year 10, and it fixes the process now: an independent appraisal sets the price at fair market value at the time of sale. Agreed in writing, before the first rent check, before anyone has leverage.

4

The lease years.

You see patients. We own the building, the debt, and the landlord obligations. Your rent is fair market plus a small premium, and the premium is the price of your option.

5

Year 5 or year 10.

Your option becomes exercisable. It is a right, not an obligation. Three outcomes, all of them yours to choose.

Buy

Exercise the option. An independent appraisal sets the price at fair market value at that time, you close, and the deed is yours. Your practice finally owns its ground.

Renew

Not ready at year 5, or the timing is wrong. Renew the lease, and the year 10 option stands on the terms written into your documents.

Walk

Plans changed. Let the option lapse and finish out your lease, the same as any tenant. There is no penalty for not exercising, and your name was never on a mortgage.

The premium

What the premium buys.

Fair market rent
Premium

The anatomy of your rent check.

Your rent has two parts. The base is fair market rent, set by comparable buildings in your market, the same number any landlord would charge. The premium is a small percentage on top, and it is the price of your written purchase option. You see both numbers, separately, before you sign.

We won't dress it up. Over the lease years the premium is real money, and if you never exercise the option, it was the cost of keeping the choice open. What it buys is specific: no down payment, no personal guarantee, and a path to the deed that exists in writing from day one.

The option

Appraisal, not negotiation.

The option price is not negotiated when you exercise. It is set by an independent appraisal at fair market value at the time of sale. The appraiser doesn't work for us, the standard is fixed, and the process is written into your documents on day one. Neither side gets to move the number.

That means today's price is not locked, and we won't pretend otherwise. If your market rises, you pay more. If it softens, you pay less. What you never face is a landlord naming a price because they know you can't leave. The process is agreed years before anyone has leverage, and that is the entire point of it. For how to interrogate any purchase option, ours included, see how to tell whether a purchase option is real.

Questions

The fine print, in plain English.

Why wouldn't I just buy the building myself?

If you have the down payment, the certainty, and the appetite to be a landlord, you should buy the building yourself. Buying is the cheaper path over 30 years for the capitalized and certain, and we'll tell you so on the call. Medre exists for everyone who isn't there yet: the owner whose capital belongs in the practice, whose lender wants a personal guarantee, or whose five-year picture isn't clear enough to bet a mortgage on.

What does the premium actually cost?

The premium's exact cost depends on the building, the market, and the lease terms, which is why the first thing we do on a call is run your numbers. It is a small percentage above fair market rent, stated separately, and you see the exact figure before you sign anything.

What's the catch?

The premium is the catch, and it's on the front page of this site. We earn the premium on your rent, and we keep good medical buildings when practices choose not to buy. Both outcomes work for us, which is why the option is real and not a teaser.

Is this a sale-leaseback?

If you already own your building, yes: selling it to Medre and leasing it back is a sale-leaseback, with one difference that matters: a written buyback option at year 5 or year 10, priced by independent appraisal. Most sale-leaseback buyers are institutions that intend to keep the building forever; the lease is the product. Ours ends, if you want it to. If you don't own a building, the structure is simpler than the term: we buy the building you need, you lease it, and the same option applies. The full transaction is unpacked in the sale-leaseback, explained.

How is the option price set?

The option price is set by independent appraisal at fair market value at the time of sale. Here is what that means, plainly. Today's price is not locked. If your market appreciates over five years, the year 5 price will be higher than today's, and if it softens, lower. What the structure removes is negotiation. No landlord naming a number, no discount for us, no markup for you. The appraiser is independent, the standard is fair market value, and the process is written into your documents before the lease starts. If a locked price matters more to you than a clean process, this is not your structure, and we'll say so on the call.

What if I can't get financing at year 5?

If you can't get financing at year 5, you renew, and the year 10 option stands on the terms already in your documents. More years of practice revenue and history can strengthen a loan application the second time, though no financing outcome is guaranteed, by us or any lender.

What happens if I walk away?

If you walk away, you finish your lease on its terms and leave, the same as any tenant. There is no penalty for letting the option lapse. The premium you paid was the price of the option you chose not to exercise.

Who handles maintenance and repairs?

Medre owns the building, the debt, and the landlord obligations. The lease spells out the maintenance and repair split the way any commercial lease does, and you'll read every line of it with your attorney before signing.

What if I sell my practice before the option date?

Whether the option survives a practice sale is written into your documents before you sign, not improvised later. Bring it up on the call. It is one of the five terms we think you should interrogate in any option, ours included.

Do I need a lawyer for this?

Yes, you need a lawyer for this. Bring your attorney and your accountant, and have them read everything. The structure survives scrutiny. That's the point of it.

Where does Medre operate?

Medre is based in Colorado and works with practices nationwide. The structure doesn't depend on geography; the building, the market rent, and the appraisal are all local to you. If your town has a building your practice needs, bring us the town.

Who am I actually dealing with?

You are dealing with two equal partners, both investing in real estate since 2009. Erika Christiansen, a licensed Colorado commercial real estate broker, and Steve Christiansen, MD, a practicing retina specialist who runs a multi-location practice. You deal with us directly on every deal, start to finish. There is no intake team.

Now bring us your numbers.

A 30-minute call with the founders. Bring your lease, your renewal terms, or the town you want to practice in. We'll tell you whether this pencils for your situation, including if the answer is no.
